items.headline: Researchers eye AI revolution in natural disaster forecasts
items.excerpt: Swiss researchers are pairing roughly 100 petabytes of NASA Earth-observation and climate data with supercomputing to train AI models that cut forecast turnaround to minutes. The goal is spotting precursors of floods and glacier collapses that physics-based models miss.

items.headline: How AI can help with early schizophrenia diagnosis
items.excerpt: Speech carries subtle acoustic and semantic markers of psychosis onset, and researchers are testing whether models can hear those differences earlier than human psychiatrists. The piece weighs the clinical upside against the risk of premature labeling.

items.headline: AI has finally come for math—mathematicians might never recover
items.excerpt: After a summer of AI-assisted proofs, mathematicians are openly debating what remains distinctly human about their craft. The reporting tracks how proof-assistant workflows and reasoning models are reorganizing the discipline's daily practice.

items.headline: How introverted or extroverted you are may influence how you use AI
items.excerpt: New behavioral research links personality traits to how people prompt and rely on generative AI, with introverts and extroverts adopting measurably different strategies. The finding suggests one-size-fits-all AI interfaces leave capability on the table.

items.headline: AlphaGenome Atlas: a predictive map of every possible DNA letter change in the human genome
items.excerpt: DeepMind released predictions for the molecular effects of 9 billion single-nucleotide variants — every possible one-letter change in the human genome — across coding and non-coding regions. Researchers can now look up a variant's predicted regulatory impact instead of running it themselves.

items.headline: AI trained to 'think' like human pathologists may be better at spotting cancer
items.excerpt: Pathology-o3 was trained on pathologists' actual search behavior — how they pan and zoom across a slide — rather than on pre-cropped regions. It flagged 100% of cancer-positive slides in testing, with a deliberately tolerated 15.5% false-positive rate.

items.headline: Earth From Orbit Is Unpredictable and Messy. Could 'Liquid' AI Clear the View?
items.excerpt: Clouds, sun angle and irregular revisit times confuse standard deep-learning pipelines for satellite Earth observation. Researchers propose bio-inspired Liquid Neural Networks, whose continuous-time dynamics adapt to inconsistent input streams onboard.

items.headline: JWST Ruled Out Finding Tiny Moons Around An Exoplanet - That's Great News
items.excerpt: A JWST non-detection of exomoons sets a useful upper limit, and the authors argue machine-learning analysis of repeated observations is the path to pulling real exomoon signals out of instrumental noise. It is a template for how ML changes null results into constraints.

items.headline: Using AI to plan for climate variability in renewable energy systems
items.excerpt: An AI model trained on 30 years of meteorological data generates realistic synthetic weather years, letting planners size batteries and hydrogen storage against tail-risk conditions rather than averages. The approach surfaces failure modes that historical-average planning hides.

items.headline: How far ahead can we predict the weather?
items.excerpt: Physicists revisit the predictability limit of the atmosphere now that AI-based models match or beat numerical weather prediction at a fraction of the compute. The question is whether data-driven emulators push the horizon out or just get cheaper.

items.headline: AI Behavior Impacted by Internal Confidence Levels
items.excerpt: Google DeepMind researchers report in Nature Machine Intelligence that LLMs use internal confidence signals to decide when to abstain from answering — a form of metacognitive control paralleling humans and animals. It reframes hallucination as a calibration problem, not just a knowledge gap.

items.headline: AI-assisted imaging tool for breast cancer could tailor screening for women according to individual risk
items.excerpt: NYU Langone's NYU-DRP reads multiple years of a patient's 3D mammograms together, beating single-scan models and traditional risk scores at predicting future breast cancer. The pitch is screening intervals set per person rather than per age bracket.

items.headline: Specificity-driven protein binder design with Odin-Multi
items.excerpt: A Technical University of Denmark team optimizes one binder sequence against many target complexes at once, applying attractive objectives to on-targets and repulsive ones to off-targets. The premise: a useful binder is defined as much by what it does not bind.

items.headline: GigaPath-Flash and GigaTIME-Flash: toward population-scale discovery with efficient pathology foundation models
items.excerpt: Microsoft Research reports pathology foundation models running roughly 50x and 6x faster than their predecessors while holding accuracy, cutting the compute wall on whole-slide analysis. The claim is population-scale histopathology becomes practical, not just demo-scale.
